newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's council meets on crucial laws.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's council meets on crucial laws.

text.p: Algeria's government-appointed National Transitional Council, a quasi-parliament, on Saturday began a special session to debate and vote election and party laws, Algerian state-run radio said.

The election law sets the rules for general elections planned for the first half of the year. The 120-article law underpins a proportional voting system to further political representation, the radio said.
The party law implements principles of the Algerian constutition, which was adopted in a referendum last year. One of the main points is that it will bar Moslem fundamentalists from seeking power.
The party legislation would tighten regulations on setting up political parties. The radio said the law requires a gradual process to form political movements, but it did not elaborate.
The council will also vote on privatisation legislation to help the government speed up the still timid privatisation process in Algeria.

The session appeared as another signal that the authorities were keeping to their plan to restructure the power base in violence-torn Algeria through elections despite increased killings which they blame on Moslem guerrillas.
The session followed President Liamine Zeroual's speech on Friday night in which he said Algeria would pursue its course to elections, pluralism and democracy.
The president's televised address followed the killings of more than 200 people in the past two weeks in bombings and massacres, mostly in Algiers and surrounding villages.

Algeria has been without an elected parliament since January 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. About 60,000 people have died since then in violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against Zeroual's government forces.
